ledger.note: 1445-1450: Pachacuti conquers the Colla of the northwest Titicaca shore. The Colla-Inca war was 'between 1445 and 1450': the Colla chief waited at Ayaviri, Pachacuti went to Hatuncolla, organised Inca administration and ordered forts built, the chief Chuchic Capac was captured and the Colla Kingdom ended. The Inca crushed a Lupaca and Colla revolt c. 1473 under Topa Inca Yupanqui. Cliopatria holds only the Puno edge of the lake until 1497. The Colla-Inca war page (war 'between 1445 and 1450') says the Lupaca 'submitted after the Inca invasion'.

The List of wars page has a 'Conquest of Collasuyu' in the 1470s-1490s against the Diaguita, Huarpes, Omaguacas, Atacamas and others ('Inca victory') and a Mapuche-Inca War 1471-1530 in which the Mapuches south of the Maule kept independence. The Inca Empire page: the empire reached 'a large portion' of Chile north of the Maule River; the Battle of the Maule is 'late 15th century' in the traditional account and 1532 for Osvaldo Silva. region.text: the north under Atahualpa: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

ledger.note: 1529: Atahualpa raises the north against Huáscar. The Inca Civil War 'began in 1529, and lasted until 1532'; Huáscar was crowned at Cusco and Atahualpa gathered the northern army at Quito; Atahualpa controlled the north and Huáscar Cusco and the south. The extent of the north is the Quito highlands (the page names Quito and Tumebamba).

region.text: the highland band from Tumebamba to Cusco where the armies of Atahualpa and Huáscar fought

ledger.note: 1529: the Inca Civil War turns the highlands into a battlefield. Battles named on the page, all undated: Tumebamba, Ambato, Bonbon, Jauja, Pincos, Andaguaylas, Limatambo, Ichubamba, Vilcas, Quipaipan (January 1532 on the page, with Huáscar's capture).

region.text: the highland band from Tumebamba to Cusco

ledger.note: April 1532: Atahualpa wins. The Atahualpa page dates the battles of Mullihambato, Chimborazo and Quipaipán to April 1532; Quipaipán was the final battle: Huáscar's army was destroyed, Huáscar captured and Cusco seized by Quizquiz and Chalcuchímac (the Inca Civil War page puts Quipaipan in January 1532 and ends the war in April 1532 in its infobox); Atahualpa 'reigned from April 1532'.

region.text: the Quito highlands and Tumebamba

ledger.note: 1532 (April): the north returns to the single Inca state under Atahualpa; the Cañari who had pledged allegiance to Huáscar were massacred. The rebel faction merges into the empire.

region.text: Cajamarca, where Atahualpa was ambushed and held

ledger.note: 16 November 1532: the Spanish capture Atahualpa at Cajamarca. Pizarro reaches Cajamarca on 15 November; on 16 November the Spanish ambush Atahualpa's unarmed followers and capture the emperor; the page counts Cajamarca Spanish-held from this date.

region.text: Cajamarca

ledger.note: 26 July 1533: Atahualpa is garrotted at Cajamarca. The Atahualpa page gives 26 July 1533 in the body (baptised that month) and notes that the 29 August of its lead is a later account; the Inca Civil War and Spanish conquest pages give 29 August and the Inca Empire page 'August 1533'. Cajamarca is Spanish from here.

region.text: Cajamarca

ledger.note: 1533: Cajamarca passes to the Spanish with Atahualpa's death; Manco Inca is later installed as ruler (1533).

region.text: Cusco and its valley, the Inca heartland

ledger.note: 15 November 1533: Pizarro's force enters Cusco. Manco Inca is installed as ruler in 1533 under Spanish control (the Inca Empire page lists him as 'installed by the Spanish'); the capital is drawn contested until Manco withdraws in 1537.

region.text: Quito

ledger.note: Quito falls to Benalcázar and Alvarado. The Spanish conquest page says they found Quito largely empty of treasure (paraphrase) but gives no date; 1534 is the year of Cliopatria's Spanish shape that holds Quito.

region.text: the Rímac valley and the site of Lima

ledger.note: January 1535: Pizarro founds Lima. The central coast round the Rímac valley, with Pachacamac, passes to the Spanish; the page says nothing of the Inca there.

region.text: Cusco and its valley

ledger.note: 1537 (spring): Manco Inca withdraws from the siege of Cusco, April 1536 to spring 1537, and flees to Vilcabamba.

region.text: the empire outside the Neo-Inca State: Cliopatria's 1534 shape minus Vilcabamba

ledger.note: 1537: Manco Inca flees to Vilcabamba and the rest of the empire is Spanish. The page says Almagro seized Cusco in 1537 and that the Spanish never held Vilcabamba in the period; the extent of the Spanish hold elsewhere in 1537 is Cliopatria's (its Spanish shape covers Peru from 1540).

1537: Manco Inca founds the Neo-Inca State at Vilcabamba. 'Established in 1537 at Vilcabamba by Manco Inca Yupanqui.' Same state in the colour registry: the Inca rulers continue (Sayri Túpac 1545, Titu Cusi 1563, Túpac Amaru 1571).

1537: the seat of the Inca moves from Cusco to Vilcabamba (the infobox capital is 'Willkapampa'; the text says Vilcabamba until 1572). [Reviewer am-04, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 lowered to 2: Manco first retreated to Vitcos (Neo-Inca State page) and the Vilcabamba, Peru page dates the capital from 1539]

region.text: the Neo-Inca State round Vilcabamba

ledger.note: 1571: the vassal status ends (infobox 'Vassal of the Spanish Empire (1567–1571)'); Toledo declares war on 14 April 1572. [Reviewer am-04, 2026-10-19: event added from the page's infobox]

region.text: the Neo-Inca State round Vitcos and Vilcabamba

wars.name: Inca Civil War

zones.text: the highland band from Tumebamba to Cusco

wars.outcome: Atahualpa's northern army defeats Huáscar's, captures Huáscar (Quipaipan) and seizes Cusco; Atahualpa holds the empire from 1532.
wars.note: Battles undated on the page except Quipaipan (January 1532); the infobox ends the war in April 1532.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire

zones.text: the Neo-Inca State's land round Vitcos and Vilcabamba (4,865 km2)

wars.outcome: The Spanish take Cajamarca (Nov 1532), execute Atahualpa (29 Aug 1533), enter Cusco (15 Nov 1533), found Lima (Jan 1535); Manco Inca's revolt and the siege of Cusco (April 1536-1537) fail and he founds the Neo-Inca State at Vilcabamba (1537); Viceroy Toledo ends it in 1572.
wars.note: Acobamba 1566 (Neo-Inca infobox only). The Spanish page says Vilcabamba was 'sacked in 1539' as well as 1572 (as read). Almagro's Chile expedition (1535/1536) failed and held no land.

wars.name: Manco Inca's revolt and siege of Cusco
wars.outcome: Manco Inca besieges Cusco from April 1536 to spring 1537, then withdraws and flees to Vilcabamba (1537).
wars.note: The Inca Empire page has Manco recapturing Cusco in 1536 and the Spanish retaking it; no month beyond April 1536 is given.

certainty.note: No treaty line: the suyu frontiers and the Maule, Chinchipe and Ecuadorian limits are approximate; Cusco's own ring is the only sharp ground.
The Spanish-held points (Cajamarca, Cusco, Lima) are dated; the Neo-Inca State's limits are 'unclear' on its page.

notes:
Inca Empire row: 8 shapes reviewed plus two new keyframes (1438 start; 1537 Neo-Inca State). Dates that differ from Cliopatria: start 1438 (infobox) against 1440; end 1572 (infobox; Neo-Inca page) against 1571. Cliopatria gives the Inca Empire 1534-1539 whole and the Neo-Inca State from 1540; the Spanish dates in the pages (Cajamarca Nov 1532, Cusco Nov 1533, Lima Jan 1535, Vilcabamba 1537) put the loss five years earlier. Chimor: conquest 1470 (Chimor infobox, Chan Chan) against Cliopatria's 1482.
Not dated by any page opened (ledger events at confidence 1 use Cliopatria shape-change years): the 1450 central-Andes shape, the 1475 northern shape, the 1497 jump to the Collao, Chile, Bolivia and northwest Argentina (2.1 M km2 against the infobox's 2.0 M for 1527: sound in size, not in date), the Quito loss (1534). The Seshat page (pe_inca_emp) was tried at seshat-db.com and did not load.
The List of wars involving the Inca Empire (a list article) gives dates the state pages lack (Cajamarcas 1460s, Chachapoyas 1472, Collasuyu 1470s-1490s, Mapuche 1471-1530, northern Andes peoples 1490-1520, Colla-Inca 1445-1550, Chincha 1440-1460) and some that conflict (the northern Andes conquest 1490-1520 against Cliopatria's Quito shape of 1475; the Chincha war 1440-1460 against 'around 1480'); it is cited only where a ledger event says so. Disagreements: Huayna Capac's death 1525 (infobox) or 1527 (his page, the Civil War page, the Inca Empire body); the Chanka war 1424/25, 1430-1440 or 1438; Chimor 1470 or 'began in the 1470s'; Quipaipan January 1532 against the war's end April 1532; Almagro's departure 1535 or 1536. The Neo-Inca ruler list has a gap 1560-1563.
Civil war: modelled as a contest over the highland band Tumebamba to Cusco (1529-April 1532) with the north lost to atahualpa-faction (rebel dossier, this group) for the same years. Spanish conquest: contested points are Cajamarca (Nov 1532 to Aug 1533, then lost), Cusco (Nov 1533 to 1537), Lima and Quito (lost); the rest of the empire is lost at 1537. The Spanish dossier (group am-06) should carry the mirror events: occupation/vassal for Manco's puppet rule 1533-1536 and the gains.
Counterparts: lupaca-kingdom, colla-kingdom, aymara-kingdoms, chachapoya-culture, chincha-kingdom and atahualpa-faction are dossiers written by this group; without dossiers: Chanka confederation (Apurimac/Andahuaylas), 'northern highland chiefdoms' and 'Andean highland chiefdoms' (undated, no page names them), Shuar. Gazetteer: all names used exist (Altiplano, Quito (region), Cuzco (100 km), places Cusco, Cuenca, Ambato, Cajamarca, Jauja, Ayacucho, Callao, Quito).
Page budget: sixteen pages cited against an allowance of five (the Inca Empire, Pachacuti, Topa Inca Yupanqui, Huayna Capac, Atahualpa, Chanka-Inca War shared with cuzco, Chimor shared with chimor, Inca Civil War, Spanish conquest, Neo-Inca State, Colla-Inca war, List of wars involving the Inca Empire, and the Lupaca, Chachapoya culture, Chincha people and Aymara kingdoms pages that date those gains and are also cited by their own dossiers); the civil war and Vilcabamba are in scope of this group (orchestrator note).
